summary: Iteration 9 review: 12/15 backend tests passed. CRITICAL backend bug detected: apply_tier_overrides() crashes with dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError because pricing.CampaignTier is @dataclass(frozen=True) but server.py mutates `t.amount_cents` / `t.included_votes` in-place. This breaks the entire admin tier override feature — POST /api/admin/tiers returns 500 after any successful DB write (because the post-write apply_tier_overrides() call crashes), DELETE /api/admin/tiers/{key} returns 500 once an override exists, and the public GET /api/business/tiers returns 500 whenever any override row exists. The features that DO work: auth session race fix (no 500 on duplicate/invalid session_id), zip download, GET /api/admin/tiers when no overrides exist, validation of tier_key/amount/votes bounds, frontend bundle compiles, landing page shows 'PT-EN-FR-DE-ZH' badge (no BETA), no MVP/'Modo TESTE'/'durante o MVP' promo strings remain. Secondary latent bug also identified in admin_reset_tier (DELETE) — even after fixing the frozen-dataclass issue, the reset path imports `pricing.TIERS as DEFAULTS` which is the SAME object as the in-module TIERS, so once overrides have mutated TIERS, the 'reset to defaults' is a no-op (still serves the previously-overridden values with is_overridden=false). Recommend snapshotting defaults at import time.

critical.issue: apply_tier_overrides() (server.py:803-810) attempts `t.amount_cents = ov[...]` and `t.included_votes = ov[...]` on a frozen dataclass (pricing.py:5 `@dataclass(frozen=True)`). Raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError → 500. Fix: either remove `frozen=True` from CampaignTier OR build a runtime overrides dict instead of mutating TIERS objects.

admin_reset_tier (server.py:1628-1631) does `from pricing import TIERS as DEFAULTS` then `TIERS[k].amount_cents = DEFAULTS[k].amount_cents`. DEFAULTS and TIERS are the same dict (same module-level object), so after a prior override mutated values in-place, resetting reads back the mutated values — NOT the original pricing.py defaults. After fixing the frozen bug, reset will incorrectly leave the override values in place while flipping is_overridden→false. Fix: snapshot defaults to an immutable copy at module load (e.g., `_DEFAULTS = {k: replace(v) for k,v in TIERS.items()}`) and reset from that snapshot, OR rebuild the tier instance via `dataclasses.replace`.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Either remove `frozen=True` from CampaignTier in /app/backend/pricing.py:5, OR refactor apply_tier_overrides() in /app/backend/server.py:796-810 to replace entries via dataclasses.replace() (e.g. `TIERS[key] = replace(t, amount_cents=ov['amount_cents'], included_votes=ov['included_votes'])`). Recommend the latter — keeps frozen invariant.

FIX (CRITICAL companion): Snapshot pricing defaults before mutations. In pricing.py expose `DEFAULT_TIERS = {k: replace(v) for k,v in TIERS.items()}` (or copy.deepcopy), and have admin_reset_tier (server.py:1628) reset from that snapshot — current code resets from a self-referencing dict and so leaves the override values in place.
Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iteration9.py after the fix; the 3 failing tests (TestAdminTiersUpdate, TestAdminTiersReset, TestPublicTiersHonorsOverrides) should then all pass.
Optional hardening: add a startup test in apply_tier_overrides() that catches FrozenInstanceError to avoid a 500 cascade if pricing.py changes shape in the future.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:796-810 apply_tier_overrides() mutates a frozen dataclass — guaranteed crash whenever any override row exists in db.tier_overrides. The function is fanned out to multiple hot paths (/api/business/tiers, POST /api/admin/tiers post-write apply, POST /api/business/campaigns pre-pricing apply, /api/business/campaigns/check-payment, etc.), so this single bug also breaks campaign creation/pricing once any override has been set.

server.py:1628-1631 admin_reset_tier — the `DEFAULTS` alias is the same object as TIERS. This is a no-op reset for in-memory state. It does correctly delete the override row, so the GET response will then have is_overridden=false, but it will continue to serve the previously-overridden numbers. Tests caught this via the amount_cents/included_votes assertions on reset.
Auth session race fix (server.py:~299) verified — invalid/duplicate session_ids return 401, never 500. Idempotent path is correct.

BETA/MVP/TESTE cleanup verified via grep: no occurrences in /app/frontend/app or /app/frontend/src outside the legitimate `stripe_mode === 'TEST'` check in admin.tsx (which is functional, not promotional copy).

campaigns.tsx (line 63-67) status-switch correctly handles canceled→ELIMINADA / pending_payment→AGUARDA PAGTO / active→ATIVA / completed→CONCLUÍDA / fallback→.toUpperCase(). Bug fix verified by code inspection.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: pricing.CampaignTier is declared `@dataclass(frozen=True)` (immutable). server.py's apply_tier_overrides() (added this iteration) mutates the in-memory TIERS dict entries directly with attribute assignment, which Python rejects on frozen dataclasses with FrozenInstanceError. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/admin/tiers {tier_key:'local', amount_cents:2500, included_votes:1500} as admin → 500 (DB write succeeds, but the post-write apply_tier_overrides call raises). 2) Once any row exists in db.tier_overrides, GET /api/business/tiers returns 500. Mitigation: replace mutation with dataclasses.replace() to rebuild the tier instance, and snapshot original defaults at import time so reset is genuine.
